part.text:
The shell tool was denied, so I couldn't build and run the tests myself — but I hand-traced the algorithm against all five test cases (sizes 0–5) and it matches the expected output exactly.

## What I implemented

**`spiral_matrix.h`** — declares the function the tests expect:

```cpp
std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> spiral_matrix(uint32_t size);
```

**`spiral_matrix.cpp`** — fills the matrix by walking inward layers. It keeps four exclusive boundaries (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) and each pass writes one edge:

1. Top row, left → right
2. Right column, top → bottom
3. Bottom row, right → left (only if a row remains)
4. Left column, bottom → top (only if a column remains)

then shrinks the boundaries and repeats. The `top < bottom` / `left < right` guards before the reverse passes prevent double-writing on odd-sized inner rings, and the reverse loops use `col - 1` / `row - 1` indexing so the unsigned decrement never wraps.

I verified by hand-trace that sizes 0, 1, 3, 4, and 5 produce exactly the matrices in the tests (e.g. size 5 yields `1 2 3 4 5 / 16 17 18 19 6 / 15 24 25 20 7 / 14 23 22 21 8 / 13 12 11 10 9`).

To build and run them yourself:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
./build/spiral-matrix
```

If you allow shell access, I'm happy to run that and confirm the suite passes.
